specification.title: Managed transaction: catch a unique violation, then return normally
steps: Start a transaction with the framework's ordinary callback or context-manager API.
Write the marker `tx` and make sure the write was sent.
Insert the duplicate value 'taken' into uniq. Catch the unique violation at the application layer. Send nothing else.
Checkpoint `before-end`: report the same backend PID. Send no query.
Allow the callback or context manager to finish normally, so the framework uses its ordinary completion path.
Checkpoint `after-api`: report the same backend PID as soon as that API has returned, before any reuse.
On the same pool or connection, run one new transaction that writes the marker `reuse` and commits. Checkpoint `reuse-after-write` if that transaction starts.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the case function has returned.

invariants.statement: The run recorded the application-visible outcome and an independent database outcome that agree with each other. This invariant does not judge whether the application-visible outcome was the correct commit report. That judgment is in the research summary.

execution.description: knex.transaction(callback) and the promise returned by knex.transaction() without a callback.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A unique_violation raised by PostgreSQL inside the transaction, and caught by the application. No statement is withheld or rewritten.
fault.injection_point: After the first write, before the transaction API finishes.
fault.expected_server: The failed statement aborts the transaction unless the application has recovered through a savepoint. This variant does not create a savepoint.
fault.expected_client: The application catches 23505. The framework then finishes the transaction through its ordinary API.

knowledge: The application caught the unique violation. Whether PostgreSQL's later reply is visible depends on the driver and the framework.
